strengths: The reported results show meaningful practical gains. At 50 images per class, Table 1 reports 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus 48.7% for CDA, and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5%. Cross-architecture experiments extend the evaluation beyond the distillation backbone.

The combination of representative feature targets and per-class BatchNorm regularization is straightforward and useful. Table 4 provides a factorial ablation, with Wasserstein matching improving over cross-entropy when both use PCBN on all three datasets.

The manuscript includes repeated-run uncertainty, hyperparameter and feature-layer studies, pseudocode, implementation settings, and a code link. The underlying transport algorithm and datasets are attributed, and the supplement acknowledges inherited dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central optimization needs clearer positioning relative to established quantization methods. With one source distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized support weights, Eq. (6) reduces to the k-means objective: minimizing the average squared distance to the nearest representative. The manuscript does not explain this equivalence or compare against classwise k-means with cluster-frequency weights and identical image recovery/PCBN. Consequently, the contribution beyond standard feature clustering and inversion remains insufficiently established.

An important baseline discrepancy undermines attribution of the headline improvements. At ImageNet-1K 10 IPC, Table 1 reports SRe2L at 21.3%, whereas Table 4 reports the corresponding CE+BN configuration at 35.9%; WMDD achieves approximately 38.1–38.2%. The manuscript does not explain this 14.6-point baseline difference. Matched teacher, recovery, relabeling, and evaluation settings are needed to establish how much improvement comes from the proposed components.

The comparison against MMD does not isolate the metric. Section 5.6 retains differences in feature encoders despite removing augmentation and FKD. In particular, at 1 IPC, the squared-Wasserstein representative is exactly the class feature mean, yielding the same matching target as linear MMD under an identical encoder. Figure 4's 0.48% versus 5.77% therefore cannot establish an intrinsic metric advantage. A controlled comparison using identical representations and regularization, including a characteristic-kernel MMD baseline, is missing. Appendix B's separate loss bounds do not resolve these confounds.

The barycenter solver has consequential specification gaps. Algorithm 2 updates the weights after solving transport, then reuses the previous transport plan for the position update without explaining consistency with the new marginals. Simplex projection also permits zero weights, while the Newton update divides by those weights. Initialization, the transport weight-update step size, and handling of zero-mass supports are unspecified. These issues leave the implemented procedure and claimed convergence unclear.

The efficiency evidence is narrower than the scalability claim. Table 3 measures ImageNette at 1 IPC, where barycenter computation reduces to a class mean; Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings but provides no ImageNet-1K runtime or memory breakdown. Accounting for feature extraction, transport computation, image recovery, and relabeling at larger image budgets would substantiate the claimed minimal overhead.
